rows.label: ▶️ Continue
rows.meta_intent: Continue legitimate unfinished development autonomously from the established project state, and stop when further work is unwarranted.
gaps: The eight-character command contains no standalone scope, stop gate, or evidence standard; it only works reliably when earlier project stewardship instructions are recovered.

rows.label: 🔁 Chat broke
rows.meta_intent: Recover after a broken conversation or execution, reconcile the last verified project state, then continue only warranted unfinished work.
gaps: The phrase 'recover context and continue' does not itself state 'continue only if genuine work remains.'

rows.label: 🔄 Restore context
rows.meta_intent: Reestablish project stewardship across conversations, preserve decisions and verified progress, and resume authorized development without artificial work.
gaps: The Restore context long-form protocol says to resume development but lacks the ten explicit conditional-continuation rules present in Project init.
Repository write/commit direction depends on established tool access and actual user authorization.

rows.label: ❓ What happened?
rows.meta_intent: Explain what interrupted the work and provide the verified current project state, without automatically resuming development.
gaps: The source asks 'what happened?' but never explicitly forbids implementation changes; diagnosis-only is an inferred intention from the question.

rows.label: 🚀 Project init
rows.meta_intent: Establish responsible engineering stewardship for a new or specified project, build an evidence-backed roadmap and autonomously complete only authorized scope.
gaps: Long form is reused for new or already-existing projects; an initialized project and an adopted project have different roadmap baselines.

rows.label: 📊 Status
rows.meta_intent: Provide a concise, measurable, evidence-backed project progress report without implying further development authorization.
gaps: The literal 'progress?' specifies neither project, evidence source, baseline, nor reporting format.
A status request should not itself trigger implementation or commits.

rows.label: 🧩 Project adopt
rows.meta_intent: Adopt an existing partially completed project, reconstruct and preserve its history, reconcile its roadmap, and finish only genuine remaining work.
gaps: The catalog situation for project inception (SITU-0014) is not equivalent to adopting an existing partially completed project; there is no selected canonical adoption-specific trigger.

rows.label: 🛠️ Fix issue
rows.meta_intent: Diagnose and repair a specifically reported defect through reproducible evidence, a scoped root-cause fix, and verified non-regression.
gaps: Selected existing situations cover implementation changes and CI failures but not the general trigger 'user reported reproducible software defect.'
A live reproduction may be impossible without local runtime, hardware or private input.

rows.label: 🔎 Gap audit
rows.meta_intent: Audit an existing project against its original objective, identify legitimate gaps, correct unsupported progress claims, and advance remediation only when warranted.
gaps: This is an active audit-and-remediation command, unlike verification-only U or status-only K.

rows.label: 🧪 Verify work
rows.meta_intent: Independently check the assistant's latest project claims against inspectable evidence, correct unsupported claims, and avoid unnecessary code changes.
gaps: The short command is strongest as a read-only verification request; 'correct claims' should not be mistaken for authorization to rewrite implementation.
